question_set.question: Use calculate_correlation with method equal to pearson and use identify_clusters with n_clusters equal to 3, method equal to kmeans in order to know What patterns can you observe in the relationship between session duration and calories burned across different workout types?

answer.value: Several key patterns emerge: 1) There is a very strong positive correlation (r=0.908) between session duration and calories burned, meaning longer sessions consistently burn more calories, 2) All four workout types show similar strong correlations (0.885-0.919), indicating this relationship holds across different exercise modalities, 3) Average calories burned are similar across workout types (884.5-925.8), suggesting workout type has less impact than duration, 4) High-frequency trainers (>=4 days/week) burn significantly more calories on average (1067.6 vs 726.4 for low-frequency trainers), 5) The data shows that session duration is the primary driver of calorie burn, regardless of workout type.

key_insights: Strong correlation (r=0.908) between duration and calories
Workout type has less impact than duration
Duration is primary driver of calorie burn
